text: Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD/'Gumboro') is caused by a virus that damages the immune system — affected chickens become more vulnerable to other diseases (which become harder to treat) and respond poorly to vaccination. Symptoms: reduced movement, loss of appetite, dehydration, and white diarrhea sticking to the vent feathers. Necropsy findings: hemorrhages in the thigh and breast muscle; the cloacal bursa (the virus's target organ) becomes enlarged, edematous, and filled with bloody or mucoid material acutely, or firm and shrunken (atrophic) in chronic cases. Treatment: none directly, since it is viral, but mixing antibiotics into drinking water for 10 days is recommended since the immune suppression makes secondary bacterial infection likely. Prevention: vaccination is the main control method; vaccinating breeder flocks is especially important, since it passes protective maternal antibodies to chicks that shield them from early infection.
